mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates labor market stress, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and housing starts (HOUST) drop by more than 10% month-over-month, it signals a severe demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and HOUST drop > 10% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.
